subject.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache` and automatically enable it for DeepSeek, or should the validated trailing-carrier behavior use a narrower provider-owned capability without this public negative flag?
rationale: The implementation appears correct and has live provider proof, but repository policy sets a high bar for new config/default surfaces, and the change alters existing DeepSeek payload ordering on upgrade.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow contract
options.body: Approve the key and DeepSeek-only default, then require a current-main rebase and green exact-head lint/type checks before merge.

options.title: Use a positive capability
options.body: Request a provider-owned or positively named implicit-prefix cache capability while retaining the proven trailing instruction carrier and explicit upgrade behavior.

options.title: Consolidate the fix
options.body: Select https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94945 as the canonical branch only after it adopts equivalent authority preservation, regression coverage, and positive real-provider proof.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow contract
recommendation.body: Approve the key and DeepSeek-only default, then require a current-main rebase and green exact-head lint/type checks before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The behavior appears to originate in their boundary-aware prompt work, so they are best positioned to decide whether this compatibility contract matches the intended architecture.
